Region Sjælland is one of the five Danish regions participating in the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD). It plays a vital role in the national quality monitoring of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) by contributing clinical data and providing leadership to the database's steering group, notably through Marianne Kajbæk Vester-Andersen, a chief physician and clinical lecturer representing the region [^src1]. 

In the period from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, Region Sjælland registered 3,897 IBD patients [^src1]. Among these, [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] accounted for 45% of the cases, while [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] made up 55% [^src1]. Additionally, the region recorded 10 patients with [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]], a severe comorbid condition [^src1]. These figures place Region Sjælland among the key contributors to the national dataset, alongside [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1].

In the subsequent reporting period, Region Sjælland demonstrated specific performance metrics in IBD diagnostics. For [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]], which evaluates the diagnostic workup for adults, the regional variation within Region Sjælland ranged from 76% to 86% [^src3]. 

Despite its active participation in data contribution, Region Sjælland formally submitted no comments or operational feedback regarding the [[danibd-aarsrapport-2024]] for the period spanning October 1, 2023, to September 30, 2024 [^src5]. This contrasts with other regions that provided detailed operational analyses or constructive criticism in their formal hearing responses to the same report [^src5].
